data.title: Make Windows VM control fast and predictable
data.body:
## Goal
- Make routine Windows VM work fast and predictable while preserving the direct host path for exact operations and guest Codex for work that needs judgment.

## Context
- Current experiments show that healthy status and direct SSH checks take about 1-11 seconds, while a guest Codex turn takes about 23-111 seconds. Manual PowerShell composition, nested quoting failures, and a broken WindowsApps shim added minutes.
- Preserve five distinct paths: direct SSH for one or two exact commands; deterministic PowerShell for exact multi-statement work; bounded guest Codex for adaptive work; managed guest Codex only for live steering; VMware Tools or the Fusion desktop for boot, SSH recovery, login, UAC, or visible state.
- Extend the existing `windows-vm-status`; do not add a second readiness command.
- Add only two runtime helpers: one deterministic PowerShell transport and one bounded Codex runner. Do not build a general remote-execution framework or a managed app-server controller.
- Keep one coordinator and one writer. Match verification evidence to the path that owns the result.
- Preserve the current uncommitted `windows-vm-control` rewrite. Do not touch the unrelated dirty `skills/claude-review/SKILL.md`.

## Performance intent
- A healthy readiness check should return immediately instead of sleeping through its wait budget.
- A direct exact command should normally finish in under 5 seconds.
- The deterministic PowerShell path should avoid guest file transfer for normal-size scripts and normally finish in under 10 seconds after the script exists.
- The bounded Codex helper should remove setup and quoting delay; model runtime remains variable and must be measured separately.

## Non-goals
- Do not automate passwords, passkeys, multifactor authentication, identity consent, unexpected UAC, or destructive VM recovery.
- Do not change Plasmite, guest credentials, MCP configuration, VM networking, or VM lifecycle as part of implementation.
- Do not add a broad test framework or promise fixed model-response latency.

data.title: Make readiness checks capability-specific
data.body:
## Goal
- Turn the existing status and doctor commands into fast, truthful readiness checks that distinguish VMware, SSH, and guest Codex capabilities.

## Context
- Work in `skills/windows-vm-control/scripts/windows-vm-status`, `guest-probe.ps1`, `windows-vmrun`, and the directly affected reference text.
- The current status probe can report a PATH-resolved Codex launcher without proving that it starts. A hard experiment found a broken `codex.cmd` while the standalone executable worked.
- `windows-vmrun doctor` currently treats Guest Operations credentials as a general blocker even when key-based SSH is healthy.
- Extend existing commands. Do not introduce another readiness or doctor executable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `windows-vm-status` accepts `--wait SECONDS` and `--require vm,tools,ssh,codex`. The explicit list overrides the default gate; `--no-ssh` conflicts with SSH or Codex requirements.
- A healthy check returns on the first successful probe. Waiting retries transient boot, Tools, route, SSH, or Codex-startup states only until the bounded deadline. Invalid configuration, missing local tools, host-key failure, and authentication failure fail immediately.
- One failed access path does not suppress an independent requested check. SSH can prove ready when Tools is unavailable; Codex readiness depends on SSH but not Guest Operations credentials.
- Codex readiness invokes `--version` in a fresh guest process. A broken PATH launcher does not mask a working supported standalone installation.
- Output names the selected executable and version without exposing secrets. Exit status reflects the requested capabilities.
- `windows-vmrun doctor` checks the wrapper, configuration, and exact VM target by default. It reports Guest Operations and VM-unlock credentials as capability notes. `--require guest-ops` and `--require vm-unlock` make those optional capabilities gate the exit result. SSH and Codex stay owned by `windows-vm-status`.
- No command starts the VM, changes routes or trusted keys, repairs Codex, or changes guest state.

## Validation Gates
- Run: `zsh -n` on the changed host scripts; exercise help, invalid arguments, immediate success, bounded timeout, broken-launcher fallback, and capability-specific doctor results with focused stubs or safe read-only probes.
- Deferred: Natural path selection and combined live timing are verified by `Forward-test the menu and measure wall time`.

data.title: Add a fast deterministic PowerShell runner
data.body:
## Goal
- Give agents a reliable path for exact multi-statement Windows work without hand-built nested quoting or routine guest file transfer.

## Context
- Add one host-side helper under `skills/windows-vm-control/scripts/`. Prefer the clear name `windows-vm-powershell` unless current conventions reveal a conflict.
- The helper reads a host `.ps1`, encodes it for the exact system Windows PowerShell executable, and runs it through one bounded SSH connection. Preserve caller stdin for the remote script.
- Keep this helper deterministic. It does not inspect, rewrite, or reason about the script.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The helper accepts an SSH alias, timeout, and exact `.ps1` path; defaults match the skill configuration where practical.
- It invokes `C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe` with `-NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand`.
- It preserves stdout, stderr, and the remote exit result. Timeout has a distinct nonzero result and a concise diagnostic.
- It rejects a missing, non-file, unreadable, or unsafe oversized payload before connecting. The error directs large exact scripts to the existing explicit copy-and-run recipe and adaptive work to bounded Codex.
- It creates no guest temporary file for supported payloads and does not log script contents or secrets.

## Validation Gates
- Run: `zsh -n`; focused stub-SSH checks for argument handling, stdin forwarding, stdout, stderr, remote nonzero exit, timeout, and oversized-input rejection; one safe live read-only PowerShell smoke on the configured VM.
- Deferred: Agent choice and end-to-end timing are verified by `Forward-test the menu and measure wall time`.

data.title: Add a bounded guest Codex runner
data.body:
## Goal
- Reduce bounded delegation to one reliable command so adaptive Windows work does not require each agent to rediscover executable paths, quoting, timeouts, Git checks, and event capture.

## Context
- Add `skills/windows-vm-control/scripts/windows-codex-run`.
- Reuse the validated Codex result from `windows-vm-status` and the deterministic PowerShell transport. Do not copy the executable-discovery or encoded-command logic into a second source of truth.
- Read the secret-free prompt from host stdin and emit the native Codex JSONL stream on stdout so the caller can inspect or `tee` it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The runner requires an exact Windows working directory and a bounded timeout. It supports optional model, reasoning-effort, and service-tier choices without inventing defaults that override the installed client.
- Trusted Git checkout is the default. A clearly named explicit flag is required for an intentional non-Git directory; the runner never silently bypasses the repository check.
- The runner starts one task-owned guest Codex process through one SSH connection, uses the exact validated executable, preserves native JSONL, and returns a useful nonzero result for readiness, SSH, timeout, or Codex failure.
- The host can recover the thread ID from the emitted stream. Process metadata goes to stderr so it does not corrupt JSONL. Timeout cleanup targets only the recorded task-owned process, and a focused check proves that the timeout does not leave an orphan.
- Prompt handling matches the documented example: host stdin is streamed to guest Codex. No guest prompt file is claimed or left behind.

## Validation Gates
- Run: `zsh -n`; focused stub checks for Git versus non-Git arguments, option quoting, prompt forwarding, JSONL preservation, timeout, task-owned process cleanup, and exit propagation; one safe live bounded run with a short read-only prompt.
- Deferred: Independent-agent usability and full timing are verified by `Forward-test the menu and measure wall time`.

data.title: Teach agents to choose and escalate control paths
data.body:
## Goal
- Make the skill state what each control path is for, how to use it well, and when to stop and move to the next path.

## Context
- Keep the selection rule and stop rules in `SKILL.md`. Put exact helper mechanics in the directly linked reference files.
- Preserve the current stored-state/live-state and evidence-boundary model. Write in simple declarative language, about halfway toward Simplified Technical English.
- Incorporate observed sharp edges only where they change action: sandboxed host access, reboot and suspend drift, broken WindowsApps launchers, intentional non-Git directories, portable exact-file checks, configured endpoint versus live-listener mismatch, and prompt streaming.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The entry point presents this order: direct SSH for one or two exact commands; deterministic PowerShell for exact multi-statement work; bounded Codex for judgment or adaptive steps; managed Codex for live steering; VMware Tools or desktop for unavailable SSH or visible state.
- Each path has concrete applicable cases, a short good-use recipe, and an explicit stop or escalation rule. One failed quoting attempt, nested or multiline logic, or more than about 30 seconds of host command composition triggers escalation from direct execution.
- The docs use the new readiness, PowerShell, and Codex helpers as the canonical normal paths. They retain the explicit script-transfer recipe only for oversized exact scripts or recovery.
- The docs explain that PowerShell is an executable used by the selected path, not a service that must remain running.
- Exact-file checks use portable `Test-Path -PathType Leaf` plus an ordinary item inspection instead of unsupported `Get-Item -File`.
- Application-client diagnosis compares a sanitized configured endpoint with an independently observed listener before changing persistent client state.
- `agents/openai.yaml` remains consistent with the final skill; regenerate it only if its interface text is stale.

## Validation Gates
- Run: `uv run scripts/validate_skill.py skills/windows-vm-control`; `git diff --check`; inspect every `SKILL.md` reference link and helper command against the implemented interface.
- Deferred: Whether a fresh agent chooses the paths quickly and correctly is verified by `Forward-test the menu and measure wall time`.

- Recommend the least-permissive persistent policy that meets the user's goal. Keep passwords, passkeys, multifactor authentication, identity consent, destructive actions, and scope expansion user-owned.
- State how an update can change or invalidate the policy and how each launch can verify the active behavior without exposing secrets.

## Checkpoint

- Then ask: approve, revise, or reject these persistent guest Codex authority settings.

## Performance intent

## Non-goals

## Goal

## Context

## Acceptance Criteria
- The runner requires an exact Windows working directory and a bounded timeout. It supports optional model, reasoning-effort, and service-tier choices without overriding the installed client's authority policy.
- Trusted Git checkout is the default. A clearly named explicit flag is required for an intentional non-Git directory; the runner never silently bypasses the repository check.
- Every invocation performs Codex readiness and version validation immediately before launch. It does not reuse a cached versioned executable path across invocations.
- The runner starts one task-owned guest Codex process through one SSH connection, preserves native JSONL, and returns a useful distinct nonzero result for readiness, SSH, timeout, approval or input request, and Codex failure.
- JSONL remains unchanged on stdout. The runner observes the stream without consuming it. When Codex emits an approval or user-input request outside standing authority, stderr immediately reports the sanitized request type and thread ID, and the bounded run returns control instead of waiting for its general timeout.

## Section Rewrite Procedure
- Inventory the exact sections to replace before editing prose.
- For each section, save its exact current text to a uniquely named task-owned file under `/private/tmp`. Then remove the section from the working document. Do not consult the saved copy, Git history, or the removed-text diff during outlining and drafting.
- Write a fresh outline that states the section's purpose, required decisions, command examples, evidence rules, and stop conditions. Keep the outline separate from the old copy.
- Draft the replacement section from the outline alone. Do not restore the old structure or sentences by default.
- Only after the new draft exists, reread the saved old section. Harvest facts, safeguards, examples, or concise wording that make the new draft more accurate or useful. Integrate those items into the new structure.
- Review the completed file for duplication and coherence across section boundaries. Delete the task-owned old-section copies and outlines after harvest and validation. Do not add process notes, tombstones, or history to the skill.
- For a genuinely new section, start with the outline and fresh draft; there is no old section to save or harvest.
- Treat generated `agents/openai.yaml` metadata separately. Regenerate it only from the final skill when its interface text is stale.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The entry point presents this order: direct SSH for one or two exact commands; deterministic PowerShell for exact multi-statement work; bounded Codex for judgment or adaptive steps; managed Codex for live steering; VMware Tools or desktop for unavailable SSH or visible state.
- Each path has concrete applicable cases, a short good-use recipe, and an explicit stop or escalation rule. One failed quoting attempt, nested or multiline logic, or more than about 30 seconds of host command composition triggers escalation from direct execution.
- Reboot guidance says that Tools and SSH can recover at different times, desktop login is not required for SSH or guest Codex, and all old PID, process, and live-session assumptions are invalid. Resume guidance says to use fresh connections and recheck Tools, guest IP, SSH route, Mac VMware address, and the scoped firewall address.
- The docs use the new readiness, PowerShell, and Codex helpers as the canonical normal paths. They retain explicit script transfer only for oversized exact scripts or recovery.
- The PowerShell guidance says it is an executable, not a service. It tells direct and guest agents to use the exact system Windows PowerShell or another native tool when `pwsh.exe`, WindowsApps, PATH, quoting, or execution policy fails.
- The approved persistent guest Codex authority policy has one documented source of truth. Approval and user-input requests outside it return control immediately. Identity, credentials, destructive actions, and scope expansion remain user-owned.
- MCP or similar client drift is checked in this order: sanitized stored client configuration, environment-variable presence in a fresh client process, configured endpoint versus independently observed listener, authentication result without exposing secrets, then one harmless application-level operation.
- When two independent paths are slow or commands start and stall, run a conditional read-only resource check through the deterministic PowerShell path. Check free disk, CPU and memory pressure, pending Windows Update or reboot state, Defender activity, and runaway processes. Report the cause; do not kill unrelated processes, disable security, or change update state automatically.
- Exact-file checks use portable `Test-Path -PathType Leaf` plus an ordinary item inspection instead of unsupported `Get-Item -File`.
- The final prose stays about halfway toward STE. It uses short direct sentences and consistent terms without losing technical precision.
- The final prose is concise and internally coherent. It does not duplicate detailed mechanics between `SKILL.md` and a reference.
- `agents/openai.yaml` remains consistent with the final skill; regenerate it only if its interface text is stale.

Re-evaluate after every Codex update because supported keys, defaults, and sandbox behavior can change. - The user approved a broad policy for this semi-disposable test VM: `approval_policy = "never"` and `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`. This deliberately permits unrestricted local command execution and network access without approval prompts.
- Keep passwords, passkeys, multifactor authentication, identity consent, broad deletion, and scope expansion as explicit agent stop rules. The approved sandbox policy does not technically enforce those semantic boundaries.
- Revalidate the installed version and effective policy after every Codex update. The inspected build was standalone Windows ARM64 `0.145.0`; `0.146.1` was available at approval time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The runner requires an exact Windows working directory and a bounded timeout. It supports optional model, reasoning-effort, and service-tier choices without overriding the installed client's authority policy.

- Every invocation performs Codex readiness and version validation immediately before launch. It does not reuse a cached versioned executable path across invocations.

- The runner starts one task-owned guest Codex process through one SSH connection, preserves native JSONL, and returns a useful distinct nonzero result for readiness, SSH, timeout, unexpected approval or input request, and Codex failure.

## Validation Gates
- Run: `zsh -n`; focused stub checks for Git versus non-Git arguments, option quoting, prompt forwarding, JSONL preservation, changed executable paths, authority-policy drift, synthetic approval and input events, timeout, task-owned child cleanup, and exit propagation; one safe live bounded run with a short read-only prompt.

User approved the broad persistent authority model for the semi-disposable Windows test VM: approval_policy=never and sandbox_mode=danger-full-access. This optimizes for speed and minimal interruption with unrestricted local commands and network access.

Passwords, passkeys, MFA, identity consent, broad deletion, and scope expansion remain agent-instruction stop rules rather than sandbox-enforced barriers. Updated dependent task K7JEZN to verify the effective policy on every launch, fail on drift after updates, and surface any unexpected approval or user-input event.

Completed the read-only spike without changing guest Codex configuration, credentials, Windows security settings, or VM state.

Implemented capability-specific readiness in windows-vm-status with --wait and --require vm,tools,ssh,codex, independent SSH probing, transient retry bounds, hard trust/auth failure handling, and explicit Codex executable/version evidence.

Updated guest-probe.ps1 to launch each Codex candidate with --version and fall back from a broken PATH launcher to the newest working standalone release. Updated windows-vmrun doctor so Guest Operations and VM unlock credentials are notes unless explicitly required.

Validated zsh syntax, help and invalid arguments, live immediate Codex success, SSH success with a failed VMware probe, fast authentication and unresolved-host failures, a 2-second bounded retry, broken-launcher fallback to standalone 0.145.0, and doctor default 0 versus required-capability 78. git diff --check passes.

Added executable windows-vm-powershell: one exact host .ps1, UTF-16LE EncodedCommand, exact system Windows PowerShell, one bounded SSH connection, preserved stdin/stdout/stderr/exit status, and no guest temporary file.

Added strict local validation for absolute .ps1 files, positive timeout, readability, regular-file type, and a 10,000-byte safe payload limit with explicit copy-and-run or bounded-Codex guidance for larger work.

Validated zsh syntax and argument errors; stubbed stdin/stdout/stderr, exit 7 propagation, timeout exit 124, and oversized exit 65; live read-only smoke returned BBOOK-WIN identity and caller stdin in 0.48s. git diff --check passes and task-owned temp fixtures were removed.

Implementation reached the approved authority-policy mutation, but host approval rejected it pending explicit user consent to the exact persistent settings and blast radius. No guest command ran and no guest configuration changed.

Required confirmation: apply approval_policy=never and sandbox_mode=danger-full-access to C:\Users\sando\.codex\config.toml. This removes Codex command approvals plus filesystem/network sandboxing for guest Codex sessions, allowing arbitrary commands and any read/write/delete/network action available to user sando. Identity, credential, destructive, and scope boundaries would remain instructions only.

Implemented the bounded runner in the correct workspace. It resolves fresh readiness, requires an exact working directory, verifies policy drift, streams prompt input and JSONL output, observes approval/input events, maps timeout and failure codes, and guards Git checkout selection.

Validated zsh syntax, stubbed prompt forwarding, option propagation, JSONL preservation, policy failure, approval and input events, timeout mapping, and exit propagation. Live SSH/Codex readiness passed, but the guest policy remains OnRequest/restricted; host approval rejected the requested persistent policy mutation, so the live bounded run remains blocked.

Completed the correct-workspace control-path implementation. SKILL.md now selects direct SSH, deterministic PowerShell, bounded Codex, managed Codex, and VMware/desktop in order with explicit stop rules. References document capability-specific readiness, reboot/suspend drift, process-local environment, portable exact-file checks, the PowerShell executable fallback, conditional resource checks, MCP/client drift, policy single-source-of-truth, and JSONL prompt streaming. Validated syntax, diff whitespace, links, live SSH, live PowerShell, runner stubs, and task-owned cleanup. The validator could not install uncached PyYAML because network access is unavailable. Full bounded Codex and independent-agent timing remain gated by the guest policy mismatch.

Forward-test is blocked by the guest Codex authority precondition, not by path selection. Fresh host-authorized evidence: direct SSH whoami completed in 0.28s; deterministic read-only PowerShell completed in 0.55s and returned BBOOK-WIN, bbook-win\sando, and C:\Users\sando; windows-vmrun doctor passed. windows-vm-status --require codex found codex-cli 0.145.0 but codex_policy=mismatch because the installed effective policy is OnRequest/restricted. windows-codex-run stopped before launch with exit 72 and authority=policy-check-failed. Focused runner stubs covered prompt forwarding, option propagation, JSONL preservation, non-Git opt-in, approval/input events, failure mappings, and host-visible task-child cleanup. The validator could not run because PyYAML is uncached and network access is unavailable. A fresh-agent trial, resource-pressure branch, full bounded run, and comparison with prior timing runs remain pending until the exact approved guest policy is present.

Review fixes: SSH-only readiness now skips all Codex work, and policy mismatch is a hard failure. Live SSH-only timing improved from 1.90s to 0.52s; a five-second Codex wait stopped after one policy probe. Focused regressions pass.

Review fix: the deterministic PowerShell runner now limits the actual encoded command to 7,000 characters before connecting. The focused regression proves an oversized script exits 65 without invoking SSH; the live synthetic process-tree check also passed.

Completed after explicit user approval of the persistent guest policy. Fixed WindowsApps launcher exit-status capture and PowerShell prompt forwarding; the runner now reads finite host stdin before asynchronous transport and passes it through the PowerShell input channel without a guest prompt file. Focused regressions pass. A live bounded read-only run returned native JSONL, identified BBOOK-WIN, exited 0, and completed in 12.25s.
